For FTTH (Fiber to the Home) internet access, the primary protocols used are:

## **GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network)**
- Most common protocol worldwide
- Provides up to 2.5 Gbps downstream / 1.25 Gbps upstream
- Uses ITU-T G.984 standard
- Single fiber shared among multiple users (typically 32-64)

## **EPON (Ethernet Passive Optical Network)** 
- Based on IEEE 802.3ah standard
- Popular in Asia, especially Japan and South Korea
- 1 Gbps symmetric speeds (can be asymmetric)
- Uses Ethernet frames natively

## **XG-PON/XGS-PON**
- Next-generation GPON
- XG-PON: 10 Gbps down / 2.5 Gbps up
- XGS-PON: 10 Gbps symmetric
- Backward compatible with GPON

## **Active Ethernet (Point-to-Point)**
- Dedicated fiber per customer
- Can deliver very high speeds (1-100 Gbps)
- More expensive but better performance
- Common in some European countries

The choice depends on the ISP's infrastructure, regional preferences, and required speeds. GPON dominates globally due to its cost-effectiveness and adequate performance for most residential users.
